I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern of winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the system I trust most here because it matches local heat, rainfall, irrigation conditions, and machinery. At my age, I want a plan that is stable, highly mechanized, and not too labor-intensive, but I also have enough education to manage inputs carefully instead of farming by habit alone. I will use improved winter wheat seed for yield stability and disease resistance, and hybrid summer maize for stronger yield potential. I will avoid spreading myself across too many crops because that raises marketing and management risk without giving me a clear advantage.

For management, I will aim for steady, controlled input use rather than chasing extreme yields. On wheat, I will focus on strong stand establishment, one good base fertilizer program, irrigation at the key stages, and limited but timely pesticide use for weeds, aphids, and disease pressure if it appears. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize and use no-tillage direct seeding where possible to save time and conserve moisture. On maize, I will push population and nutrients enough for good yield, but I will still keep costs disciplined and rely on 1 to 2 well-timed irrigations depending on rainfall. Overall, I will choose the wheat-maize double-cropping system because it gives me the most reliable income, fits Hebei conditions, and lets me manage the farm efficiently with lower uncertainty.
